QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_14

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil is assessing two proposed fundraises: (X) Asha Deep Trust plans a ZCZP public issue for a women-empowerment project; (Y) a consortium of three NPOs plans a Development Impact Bond for literacy outcomes across 3 states. The MOST material difference for her impact-assessment approach is:

answer.text: Both are identical in treatment; the SIA applies the same SAS-200 indicators to both.
The ZCZP requires no impact measurement because there is no return; the DIB requires full measurement because it is pay-for-success.

The DIB is outcome-linked (payments released only on verified outcomes against pre-agreed metrics) requiring outcome-verification rigour, while the ZCZP is donation-based (funders expect social impact but payment is upfront and non-returnable), requiring output/outcome tracking but no pay-for-success gating.
The ZCZP is settled on stock exchanges while DIBs are off-market bilateral contracts with no listing possibility.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.64 and 68-70, DIBs are pay-for-success instruments where payment is released only on verified achievement of pre-agreed outcome metrics. ZCZPs (see p.158) are upfront zero-coupon zero-principal instruments where funders expect social returns and the issuer carries AIR and reporting duties, but there is no pay-for-success gating on funds released. The Trap: Option A ignores the pay-for-success gating that distinguishes DIBs. Option B wrongly claims ZCZPs need no impact measurement — they do, for the Annual Impact Report. Option D wrongly says DIBs cannot be listed on the SSE. Note: The core distinction is timing and conditionality of funds: DIB payments follow verified outcomes, while ZCZP funds are received upfront with social-return reporting obligations.
